# Disagreement Log — Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 23

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Chapter:** POX 23 — Discovery of Zechariah's blood; mourning; Simeon appointed

---

## Disagreements

**1. 23:1 — "congealed blood"**
- EMET: "congealed blood"
- LOGOS: "congealed blood"
- PNEUMA: "dark, coagulated blood, pooled beside the altar"
- Note: Greek *haima pepēgos* = "congealed/hardened blood." EMET/LOGOS are accurate. PNEUMA adds "dark" and "pooled" — descriptive additions not in the Greek.

**2. 23:1 — "his blood shall not be wiped away"**
- EMET: "his blood shall not be wiped away until his avenger comes"
- LOGOS: "His blood will not be wiped clean until his avenger comes"
- PNEUMA: "His blood will cry out from this place until the one who comes to avenge him arrives"
- Note: Greek *ou smagestai ews hēxē ho ekdikos autou* = "shall not be wiped/blotted until his avenger comes." PNEUMA adds "will cry out from this place" — an addition from Gen 4:10 (*"your brother's blood cries out"*) not in the actual Greek of this verse.

**3. 23:2 — "wainscotings of the temple cried out"**
- EMET: "the wainscotings of the temple cried out"
- LOGOS: "The wainscoting panels of the temple cried out in lamentation"
- PNEUMA: "The carved wooden panels of the sanctuary walls groaned and cried out"
- Note: Greek *ta katapetasmata tou naou* — some MSS have *katapetasmata* (veils/curtains) rather than *kosmēmata* (decorations/paneling). This is a significant textual variant. If "curtains," the reference may be to a tearing similar to Mark 15:38.

**4. 23:2 — "they rent their garments from the top to the bottom"**
- EMET: "from the top to the bottom"
- LOGOS: "from top to bottom"
- PNEUMA: "from neck to hem"
- Note: Greek *apo anōthen heōs katō* = "from above to below." EMET/LOGOS preserve the directional language; PNEUMA's "neck to hem" is accurate but loses the vertical cosmological imagery.

**5. 23:3 — "his blood turned to stone"**
- EMET/LOGOS: "his blood turned to stone"
- PNEUMA: "his blood — hardened into stone"
- Note: Greek *to haima autou eis lithon metatraphenta* = "his blood turned/transformed into stone." All three render this correctly; minor stylistic variation.

**6. 23:4 — "saw the Christ in the flesh"**
- EMET: "until he had seen the Christ in the flesh"
- LOGOS: "until he had seen the Christ in the flesh"
- PNEUMA: "before he had seen the Messiah with his own eyes"
- Note: PNEUMA drops "in the flesh" (*en sarki*) — theologically important because this phrase echoes the anti-docetist formula of 1 John 4:2 ("Jesus Christ has come in the flesh"). EMET/LOGOS preserve it.
